elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 3(i) as rendered now reads "Client may, but is not required to, order from TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface" — the mandatory "Client shall order" requirements tie is gone, leaving a pure option. Nothing else in the rendered text imposes a requirements or sole-supplier duty on Client: Section 2(a) expressly confirms Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize" similar third-party software and services, and Section 13 imposes only term/renewal mechanics. Deterministic check "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" returned ok.; the surviving "non-exclusive" grant language runs in Client's favour.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: its condition does not apply because, after the edit, no exclusivity obligation binds Client at all (Section 3(i) is now permissive: "may, but is not required to, order"). A scope limitation is therefore unnecessary; the preferred position (no exclusivity) subsumes it.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element with no operative trigger: there is no exclusivity to time-limit. Section 13's indefinite one-year auto-renewals no longer extend any sourcing commitment because the only such commitment (Section 3(i)) has been made optional.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no performance-based exit is required where Client carries no exclusivity. Client's freedom to source credit reports elsewhere is now unconditional and does not depend on TrueLink's service-level performance.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: not applicable for the same reason — the operative language creates only an option to order, so no delivery-failure termination trigger is needed to release Client.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single preferred element is satisfied by operative language, not merely promised in the comment — "shall order" has been replaced with "may, but is not required to, order from TrueLink," which eliminates the 100%-of-requirements tie for credit reports in the Interface channel.

Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because the preferred position removes exclusivity entirely; no product-category, 12-month, or performance-exit language is needed. The comment's offer of a capped-exclusivity fallback is a negotiating position only and is correctly left out of the operative text.

Minimal: a single phrase in Section 3(i) changed (plus the necessary "order from TrueLink" grammatical fix). TrueLink's affirmative duty to transmit credit data, the "Subject to the foregoing" qualifier, and TrueLink's no-representation/no-liability disclaimer all survive verbatim; Sections 2(a) and 13 are untouched, and the favourable existing language (non-exclusive licence to Client, Client not obligated to utilize the License) is retained.

Preserves intent: term, renewal, and termination mechanics in Section 13, the Credit Repository/Credit Bureau Agreement conditionality, and the nonexclusive Credit Data licence in Section 8(d) are unaffected; no new obligation is imposed on either party and no remedy or timing provision is contradicted.

Residual drafting nit (not a defect requiring repair): with the obligation now permissive, the trailing words "on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface" read as a description of scope rather than a duty. If TrueLink pushes back, the phrase could be tightened to "may order from TrueLink credit reports on borrowers submitted for underwriting approval through a System using the Interface," but the current text is unambiguous that no order is required.

Verification scope note: the deterministic scan and my review cover the cited and rendered paragraphs only. Before sending, confirm no other sourcing/volume-commitment language (e.g., minimum volumes or fee schedules assuming all reports run through TrueLink) sits elsewhere in the agreement, which would need the same treatment.

Severity confirmed at high pre-redline: the original Section 3(i) was full-term exclusive dealing (running through indefinite one-year renewals) with no performance-based exit, i.e. walk-away territory. Section 2(a) and the 30-day non-renewal right mitigate but do not cure, because exiting the tie would require abandoning the whole service.
